lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Good morning! What would you like?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: I would like a sandwich and a coffee, please.

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Would you like milk in your coffee?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Yes, please. And a glass of water.

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Anything else?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: No, thank you. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: That is eight dollars.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Here you are.

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Thank you. Have a nice day!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hi, Leo. It's Mia. Do you have the math homework?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes. We have to do page twelve, exercises one and two.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Thanks. Do you want to study together?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Sure. Let's meet at the library at five.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: OK. See you at five. Bye!

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Bye!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Hi, Nina! How was the beach?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: It was great! The weather was sunny and warm.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: What did you do there?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: I swam in the sea and found a small shell.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Nice! Did you take photos?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Yes, I did. I can show you on Monday.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Great. What time did you go home?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: We went home at five o'clock.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hi, Alex. Are you free next weekend?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: No, I'm not. I'm going to visit my grandparents.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Oh, nice. What are you going to do there?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: I'm going to work in the garden and walk to the lake.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: When are you going to come home?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: On Sunday evening. Do you want to play football on Monday?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Sure! Let's meet at the park at four.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Great. See you on Monday!

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Come in, Maya. You wanted to talk about your project.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes. I am studying how people use the new public space near the station.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: That is a good topic. What is your research question?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I want to know if the space changed how often people talk to their neighbors.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Interesting. How will you collect data?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I plan to interview twenty residents and count how many people use the space at different times.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Good. You should also observe the space on a weekend. The pattern may be different.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I will. When should I send you the first draft?

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: By Friday, please. Then we can meet on March 12.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: How long should the report be?

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: About five pages, not more. Focus on the evidence, not on background.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Should I include photos?

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: One or two, if they help. But do not use photos of people without permission.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Understood. I will send the questions to you before I start the interviews.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Perfect. And Maya, remember to keep a research diary. It will help you explain your choices later.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I will. Thank you, Professor Grant.
